meta.title: ProxMenux Monitor on Proxmox Backup Server | ProxMenux Documentation
meta.description: ProxMenux Monitor on a Proxmox Backup Server host: its tabs, the Overview, Datastores and Tasks pages, what changes in Network and Hardware, sign-in with the accounts of the server, the Health Monitor and the settings it hides.

header.title: ProxMenux Monitor on Proxmox Backup Server
header.description: What the Monitor shows when it runs on a Proxmox Backup Server host: tabs for datastores and tasks instead of guests and apps, sign-in with the accounts of the server, and the health checks of a backup server.

sections.title: How the Monitor knows it runs on PBS

blocks.p: The Monitor asks its own server which product the host runs (/api/platform), with the same detection as the menu, described in Detection and supported versions. The server keeps the answer for 60 seconds. On a Proxmox Backup Server host the header shows Proxmox Backup Server Dashboard under the Monitor name, and the dashboard has the tabs described on this page.

sections.title: Tabs
sections.intro: A Proxmox Backup Server host has its own tabs, always in this order. Each one appears when the profile of the account includes its area or action:

rows: The state of the host, with the datastores in place of the VMs and LXCs.
The datastores of the server, and the disks of the host.
The recent tasks and the maintenance schedules of the server.
The network tab of Proxmox VE, with one card less.
The hardware tab of Proxmox VE, without its installers.
The terminal of the host, as in the <terminalLink>Terminal tab</terminalLink> of Proxmox VE.
Every profile. System Logs needs its area.

blocks.p: The order cannot be changed: Settings has no Navigation order card on a PBS host. Network and Hardware are tabs of their own instead of entries of the Node menu, because the storage of the server is in Datastores. There are no Apps, Catalog, VMs & LXCs or Backup tabs.

sections.title: Overview
sections.intro: The Overview keeps the layout described in <overviewLink>System Overview tab</overviewLink>, with these changes:

items: The card of VMs and LXCs becomes Datastores: the number of datastores, All available or how many are unavailable, and the usage of the first two. When there are more, a line below says how many.
The storage card lists the usage of each datastore in place of VM/LXC Storage and Local Storage (System).
The system card shows PBS Version: instead of Proxmox Version:.
The history charts read the metrics the server records itself, with proxmox-backup-debug api get /nodes/localhost/rrd. Those metrics have no ZFS ARC value, so the memory chart has no ARC history.
Datastore usage turns yellow above 75 % and red above 90 %, the same thresholds as the storage of Proxmox VE. The datastore data refreshes every minute.

figure.alt: Overview tab of the Monitor on a Proxmox Backup Server host, with the Datastores card and the PBS Version line
figure.caption: The Overview of a Proxmox Backup Server host.

blocks.p: The Datastores tab has a card for each datastore of the server, read with proxmox-backup-manager datastore list. Each card shows the name, the status (active or error), the percentage used, Total, Used and Available, and the path of the datastore. The capacity is that of the filesystem holding the path. The data refreshes every 30 seconds.
A datastore in maintenance mode, or a removable one whose device is not mounted, shows The datastore is offline, in maintenance mode or its backing device is not mounted. in place of its capacity.
Below the datastores come the disks and pools of the host, as in the <storageLink>Storage tab</storageLink> of Proxmox VE, without its summary cards and its list of Proxmox storages.

figure.alt: Datastores tab with one card per datastore showing its status, usage, total, used and available space and path, and the disks of the host below
figure.caption: The Datastores tab.

blocks.p: The Tasks tab has two tables, refreshed every 30 seconds:

rows: The last 20 tasks of the server, from proxmox-backup-manager task list: the type (backup, restore, verification, prune, garbage collection, sync and others), the start time, the duration and the result.
The sync, verification and prune jobs, with their datastore, their schedule and the result of their last run. With none configured, it shows No sync, verification or prune schedules are configured.

figure.alt: Tasks tab with the Recent tasks table and the Maintenance schedules table
figure.caption: The Tasks tab.

sections.title: Network and Hardware
sections.intro: These tabs are those of Proxmox VE, described in <networkLink>Network tab</networkLink> and <hardwareLink>Hardware tab</hardwareLink>. On a Proxmox Backup Server host:

items: Network has no Network Flow card, which draws how traffic reaches the VMs and LXCs.
Hardware has no Switch Mode control for GPUs, no driver installers and no Extended Monitoring Not Available notice. The Run scripts and tools action adds nothing to this tab.

sections.title: Signing in
sections.intro: Local accounts, profiles, 2FA and API tokens work as described in Access & Authentication. The Proxmox accounts that can sign in are those of the backup server. They are turned on in the Proxmox Backup Server accounts card of Security, which works as described in Proxmox VE accounts. What changes:

items: When local accounts can also sign in, the login screen has two tabs, Local account and Proxmox Backup Server. Otherwise it shows only the form of the server. The form has User, Password and Realm, and the realms are those the server lists. When the account has a second factor, Two-factor code takes a TOTP code or a recovery key.

The privileges on / of the server decide, as on Proxmox VE: Sys.Modify gives Administrator and Sys.Audit alone gives Observer, unless a rule gives another profile. Without either one the account cannot sign in.

An account whose only second factor is a security key signs in on the web interface of the server, on port 8007. With the Monitor opened over HTTPS at the same address, that session also signs in to the Monitor.
Proxmox Backup Server has no user groups, so a profile rule names a user.

A custom profile chooses among the areas Overview, Datastores, Tasks, Network and hardware and System Logs, and the actions Run scripts and tools, Update and Open terminals. Profiles are described in Users and profiles.

figure.alt: Login screen of the Monitor with the Local account and Proxmox Backup Server tabs, the second one selected with its User, Password and Realm fields
figure.caption: Signing in with an account of the server.

sections.title: Health Monitor
sections.intro: The <healthLink>Health Monitor</healthLink> checks what a backup server has:

items: PBS services checks proxmox-backup and proxmox-backup-proxy instead of the Proxmox VE services, and never corosync.

The checks of VMs and LXCs, of Proxmox VE storages and their capacity, of LXC root disks and mount points and of VM disks do not run. The remote NFS, CIFS and SMB mounts of the host are still checked.
Health Monitor Thresholds in Settings hides the thresholds of those checks.

In System updates, when updates are pending, the Update system button opens a terminal window with pbs_update.sh, the update of option 6 of the PBS menu, described in Updating the server. It needs the Update action.

sections.title: Settings, Security and Admin
sections.intro: The Admin menu has no Audit & Report, and the welcome carousel and the release notes window of the Proxmox VE Monitor do not open. These parts of the Settings tab and the Security tab are not shown on a Proxmox Backup Server host:

rows: Navigation order, Remote Storage Exclusions, LXC Update Detection, GitHub API, Notifications, Snippets storage, and the VMs & Containers row of the Health Monitor suppression durations.
The Proxmox VE group: Firewall, Fail2Ban and Lynis security audit.
